newsitem.title: NEPAL: South Asian nations to start talks next week.
newsitem.headline: South Asian nations to start talks next week.

text.p: Senior officials from South Asian nations will begin a third round of talks next week in the Nepali capital on tariff cuts intended to boost trade in the region, officials said on Friday.

"This round will enlarge the schedules of items for tariff cuts under SAPTA (South Asian Preferential Trading Arrangement) by adding more products in the list," an official of the South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC) said.

The official said the third round of negotiations is expected to be completed before December this year when the commerce ministers from the region meet in Karachi to discuss liberalization of trade in South Asia, home to one-fifth of the world's population.
Member countries of SAPTA during the first and second rounds of talks, have agreed on a list of more than 1,800 primary, manufactured and consumer goods for tariff cuts between 10 and 100 percent.
The least developed member countries are entitled to additional tariff cuts on a non-reciprocal basis.
SAARC was formed in December 1985 to improve the economies of the region. It groups Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, the Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan and Sri Lanka.

Member countries provide tariff cuts for imports within the region under SAPTA which came into force in December 1995. They have set a goal to launch South Asian Free Trade Area (SAFTA) by the year 2001.
"This round of talks will accelerate the negotiations to attempt to cover much larger number of products," Ashok K. Attri, director of the Kathmandu-based SAARC secretariat, told Reuters.
Trade between the seven South Asian nations currently represents only 3.4 percent of the total global trade.
